hints: Represent rows and columns as the two sides of a bipartite graph.
Each coin is an edge; selecting a row or column must cover every edge.
A minimum vertex cover in a bipartite graph has the size of a maximum matching.
analogy: Cover every coin by choosing one of its two labels: its row or its column.
example: Coins at (1,1), (1,2), and (2,2) require 2 moves: remove rows 1 and 2.
algorithm: Build a bipartite graph with one vertex per row and column and an edge for every coin. Compute a maximum matching with a bipartite matching algorithm and print its size.
correctness: Moves correspond exactly to vertices covering every coin edge. By Konig's theorem the minimum vertex-cover size equals the maximum matching size, so the matching gives the optimum.
complexity: For n rows and columns and E coins, Hopcroft-Karp takes O(E*sqrt(n)+n) time and O(n+E) space.
